absorptions.upstream_title: Reconnect MCP servers on explicit refresh (#35151)
absorptions.semantic_mapping: Hepta's explicit refresh queues a complete configuration for the next turn. Every consumed request constructs a new McpConnectionManager without a previous-manager reuse input, atomically swaps it into the session, cancels the preceding startup generation, and shuts down the old manager. The upstream stale-connection bug therefore does not exist on this narrow local path.

behavioral_evidence.assertion: Two consecutive explicit refresh requests each cancel the preceding startup token and install a fresh uncancelled generation.
A real Apps Streamable HTTP transport receives a second initialize request after an explicit same-configuration refresh.

non_claims: An idle thread does not immediately replace its MCP manager; the queued refresh is consumed at the next turn boundary.
A cancelled or failed replacement does not restore the consumed refresh intent.
Hepta does not implement upstream ordinary-update connection reuse because it does not yet own the published McpRuntime architecture.
This equivalence does not absorb the R6 published-runtime, authentication-generation, or same-generation exposure and execution prerequisites.

deferrals.upstream_title: Reconnect MCP servers on explicit refresh (#35151)
deferrals.reason: The full upstream commit also preserves a reconnect request when a runtime replacement is cancelled and assumes the R6 published immutable runtime. Hepta still lacks serialized refresh ownership, desired and applied generations, authoritative authentication generation, immutable publication, and a generation-bound tool catalog plus executing client. Directly copying the AtomicBool reconnect flag would place ownership in the wrong layer and would not close stale-credential or mixed-generation races.
missing_prerequisites: recoverable refresh intent across cancellation and parse or startup failure
latest desired configuration and environment snapshot
generation-bound tool catalog and executing MCP client
required_behavioral_tests: An idle-thread refresh denies new calls through the old generation until the replacement is ready.
Cancellation at every replacement await point preserves the refresh intent and eventually reconnects.
Concurrent explicit, configuration, and authentication refreshes publish only the highest valid generation.
Account rotation or logout cannot emit the prior Authorization header or expose the prior account's catalog.
Tool exposure and execution resolve through one immutable client and catalog generation.
Invalid configuration and startup failure have explicit fail-closed behavior.
